GOLDMAN SACHS TURNS BULLISH ON STOCKS AND BONDS Goldman Sachs has upgraded equities to overweight over three months and bonds to overweight over 12 months. The bank sees improving valuations, resilient earnings and easing inflation supporting markets into 2027. Goldman favors AI-linked stocks and selective dividend plays, while warning that rising yields and geopolitical tensions could keep volatility elevated.

TRUMP'S RUSSIAN DIESEL DEAL UNLIKELY TO BRING PRICES DOWN Trump says Russia will release 4.8 million tons of diesel, equivalent to roughly 35.8 million barrels. That sounds substantial, but it would cover just nine days of U.S. diesel demand, according to EIA data. Only 300,000 tons are expected initially, while Ukrainian strikes have significantly constrained Russian refining capacity. FRANCE'S ECONOMY STALLS AS GROWTH HITS JUST 0.1% France's economy grew just 0.1% in Q3, following stagnation in Q2, according to the Bank of France. Rising energy costs, weak manufacturing and sluggish construction continue to weigh on growth. Business uncertainty is increasing, with companies delaying investments and households cutting spending. Automotive production could fall sharply in October due to supply shortages. Official Q3 GDP figures are due October 30.

Tehran accused London of fabricating allegations and orchestrating a “false flag” operation, demanding concrete evidence to support the claims. Iran also warned that the British government would bear responsibility for any consequences arising from the accusations.

HSBC: DON'T FIGHT THE AI TRADE AS STOCK RALLY GAINS MOMENTUM HSBC expects strong Q3 earnings and accelerating AI demand to extend the equity bull market. S&P 500 forward valuations have fallen 16.5% since late 2025, while earnings guidance is improving at its fastest pace since 2021. The bank favors AI hyperscalers, citing surging computing demand and resilient GPU prices. HSBC sees earnings as the next catalyst for stocks to move higher.

The denial follows a Reuters report that Trump's envoys presented the deal as an effort to bring Moscow back to peace talks. “I don't see any direct connection here,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said, calling the agreement mutually beneficial. FED'S WALLER: SURGING U.S. BOND YIELDS DRIVEN BY GROWTH, NOT INFLATION Fed Governor Christopher Waller says strong economic growth and AI investment are pushing Treasury yields higher, while inflation expectations remain anchored. He warns that weaker safe-haven demand for U.S. debt could be adding 50–70 basis points to yields. Waller expects the AI investment boom to continue for another 2–3 years.

IRAN WARNS U.S. OF MILITARY CONSEQUENCES AS OIL PRICES RISE Iranian officials have issued fresh warnings against U.S. military action, adding to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister warned that another U.S. military operation would have consequences extending beyond the region. Meanwhile, a senior IRGC commander declared that Iran is ready to respond to any new military aggression. Crude oil prices are moving higher amid the escalating rhetoric.

TRUMP WARNS HOUTHIS OVER ATTACKS ON SAUDI ARABIA AND RISING OIL PRICES President Trump accused Yemen's Houthis of attacking Saudi Arabia and deliberately trying to drive up oil prices ahead of U.S. elections. He suggested Iran may be behind the renewed attacks, while recalling previous U.S. strikes against the group. Trump issued a direct warning to the Houthis: “I'll be there after the Elections, and I will never forget!” The remarks signal a potential escalation in U.S.-Houthi tensions.

NETANYAHU, TRUMP REPORTEDLY DISCUSS RENEWED STRIKES ON IRAN Netanyahu reportedly discussed renewed military action against Iran with Trump last week, according to Axios. U.S. officials believe Netanyahu may seek strikes before Israel's October 27 elections. No military decision has been confirmed.

ZELENSKYY PROPOSES NEW TALKS WITH U.S. IN COMING DAYS Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says Ukraine has submitted proposals for further negotiations with the United States. He confirmed sending meeting proposals to Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, adding that Ukraine is ready to meet within days. “On the Ukrainian side, there is always a constructive approach.”

BOND EXPERT WARNS OF $110 BILLION SELLING SHOCK IF TREASURY YIELDS HIT 6% Veteran bond strategist Harley Bassman warns of a “nightmare scenario” in U.S. Treasuries. If the 20-year Treasury yield rises above 6%, futures-related hedging could trigger selling pressure equivalent to $110 billion in bond issuance. The 20-year yield currently stands near 5.6%. Bassman says negative convexity risks have reached levels not seen since 2007, potentially amplifying the Treasury selloff.

BITCOIN WHALES RESUME ACCUMULATION AS MARKET ENTERS EARLY BULL PHASE Large Bitcoin holders are buying again after more than a year of selling, according to CryptoQuant. Whales now hold 3.03 million BTC, their highest holdings since November 2025. CryptoQuant says the shift toward accumulation signals an “early bull phase” and improving investor sentiment. Bitcoin (bitcoin:native ) is trading near $83,045, largely unchanged on the day.

U.S. DIESEL FUTURES SURGE 4.5% DESPITE TRUMP'S RUSSIAN FUEL DEAL U.S. diesel futures jumped 4.5% to a two-week high, despite President Trump's agreement to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Energy traders warn that the additional Russian supply is insufficient to meaningfully lower fuel prices. Meanwhile, U.S. retail diesel averages $6.28 per gallon, near September's record of $6.53. Lawmakers from both parties are also questioning the deal's legality.

U.S. CORE INFLATION FORECAST ALIGNS WITH WALL STREET EXPECTATIONS The Cleveland Fed's inflation nowcast points to core CPI rising 0.20% month-over-month, nearly matching analysts' median forecast of 0.21%. Key figures: * Headline CPI: +0.53% MoM, below analysts' forecast range of 0.55%–0.62%. * Core CPI: +0.20% MoM vs. +0.21% expected.
